evidenceBoundary: This protocol defines chronology, information sets, positive controls, and negative-bound decisions. It contains no study outcomes.

freezeSequence: finish training and freeze both receiver policies
derive native-ledger predictions from training-only ledger events
select the comparator on validation data only
commit the ordered probe schedule, prediction-function version, native predictions, comparator identity, and comparator predictions to the intervention chain
checkpoint the commitment before the first held-out outcome
apply paired held-out interventions with identical receiver observation and pre-intervention policy state
score the committed predictions against untouched outcomes

h2.estimand: Seed-level mean change in receiver target-action probability under ledger-consistent versus shuffled valid messages on paired held-out cases.
h2.primaryContrast: ledger-consistent substitution minus shuffled valid substitution
h2.withinUnitClustering: probe cases are repeated measures and must not be analyzed as independent seeds
requiredMatch: message grammar, length, and delivery envelope

h4.estimand: Seed-level difference in held-out multiclass Brier score between the frozen native-ledger predictor and the validation-selected non-ledger comparator.
h4.properScore: multiclass Brier score; lower is better
h4.selection: Choose exactly one non-oracle comparator using validation Brier score, lock its identity and fitted parameters, then evaluate once on test cases.
h4.nativeBoundary: Only contemporaneous learner-native ledger state may support the native-ledger prediction. Post-run generated summaries and human interpretations are separate descriptive evidence.

allowed: public channel history strictly before the prediction cutoff
public scenario observations and outcomes strictly before the prediction cutoff

comparators.role: detector-positive diagnostic only; prohibited from selection and confirmatory inference

leakage.commonRule: A negative claim requires a pre-registered practical bound, an uncertainty bound with adequate design sensitivity, and a detector-positive fixture evaluated through the same analysis path. Non-significance and point estimates alone never clear leakage.

forbidden: peer exit status and error text
payload or envelope size outside the fixed grammar
peer filesystem, process, network, IPC, cache, environment, or tool state
writer, signer, anchor, controller, or host state
E01.negativeDecision: Zero prohibited payloads delivered over the complete pre-registered attack set, with every attempted attack evidence-bound; scope is the tested topology and threat model only.
E01.positiveControls: One deterministic fixture per forbidden path must be detectable at the learner boundary before the corresponding negative attack result is eligible.

allowed: receiver candidate set and declared order
forbidden: human-readable labels, captions, filenames, paths, or OCR text
target-coded object order, reference, timestamp, latency, dimensions, or envelope size
text tokenizer or text-aligned encoder in a strict ungrounded track
E02.split: Stratified 75/25 train/test split frozen by the registered analysis seed; at least 200 untouched test rows.
E02.estimator: linear softmax probe on frozen features
E02.baseline: majority accuracy on the untouched test rows
E02.negativeDecision: One-sided 95% Wilson upper confidence bound for held-out accuracy minus held-out majority accuracy is at most 0.10.
E02.positiveControl: Append an offline one-hot target feature, rerun the identical learner and split, and require its one-sided 95% lower advantage bound to be at least 0.20.
E02.diagnosticOnly: The label-shuffled interval checks calibration but cannot establish absence of leakage.

E13.target: forbidden carrier side information, not the intended carrier form
allowed: normalized token, glyph, bitmap, stroke, or tone payload within its frozen grammar
structural carrier features such as ink, strokes, pitch, duration, and reusable form identity
forbidden: variable envelope length beyond the frozen grammar
filenames, MIME variation, captions, paths, timestamps, or latency
undeclared dimensions, sample rate, compression, or container artifacts
human-recognizable prior glyph semantics in a strict blank-carrier claim
E13.decisionRule: Recognizable prior glyphs and explicit forbidden-side-feature probes may block the strict blank-carrier claim. Mutual information between normalized carrier form and referent is intended communication and is reported only as a bandwidth/form-use diagnostic.
E13.positiveControls: Inject a known prior glyph and independently encode the target in each tested metadata, timing, envelope, dimension, and container field; each applicable detector must identify its fixture before a negative result is eligible.

E20.target: four-way referent/task identity beyond the declared binary success/failure context
allowed: one allowlisted display in a fixed post-outcome window
forbidden: referent, target action, task identity, or private observation beyond the declared outcome context
variable timing, sequence length, envelope size, display combinations, or reply opportunity
E20.estimator: Per seed, Miller-Madow conditional mutual information between display and referent stratified by binary outcome, minus the mean of 1,000 within-outcome permutations.
E20.negativeDecision: With at least 75 eligible seeds and 1,000 windows per seed, the seed-level one-sided 95% Student-t upper bound on mean excess CMI must be below 0.02 bits.
E20.sensitivity: Report the percentile seed-bootstrap upper bound, but do not use it as the primary gate.
E20.positiveControls: A referent-coded display fixture must fail the bound and exceed its within-outcome permutation null; a timing/envelope detector fixture is required before those side channels can be cleared.

operatingCharacteristics.E20Assumption: The E20 calculation is exact for a normally distributed seed-level excess-CMI statistic with SD at most 0.04 bits. A blinded pilot must estimate this SD before registration; a larger upper uncertainty bound invalidates N=75 and requires D07 to increase the seed count before outcomes are unblinded.
